title: New America Acquisition I Corp SPAC
summary: The core claims hold up. New America Acquisition I Corp filed with the SEC on Aug. 4, 2025 for a $300M NYSE IPO, with Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump on its advisory board. The two hold 5 million founder shares, worth about $50M on paper at $10 a share. The original S-1 said the SPAC would target firms 'well-positioned to benefit from federal or state-level incentives, such as grants, tax credits, government contracts or preferential procurement programs', and an amendment filed later the same day removed that language after AP asked about it. The caveats: the IPO priced in December 2025 and closed at $345M with the over-allotment, the video's quote drops 'grants, tax credits', the 'identifiable economic or security interest' phrase could not be checked against the filing, and the idea that the sons would phone the Pentagon is the video's inference, not a documented act.

sub_claims.statement: New America Acquisition I Corp is a SPAC raising $300 million.
sub_claims.finding: This is a Florida blank-check company, ticker NWAX on the NYSE. It filed its S-1 on Aug. 4, 2025 for a $300M IPO of 30 million units at $10, each unit being one Class A share plus half a warrant with an $11.50 strike. It priced the $300M IPO on Dec. 3, 2025, and units began trading Dec. 4. With the over-allotment exercised, the closing announced Dec. 5, 2025 was for $345M (34.5 million units). The underwriters were Dominari Securities and D. Boral Capital. Kevin McGurn is chairman, CEO and CFO.

sub_claims.statement: Don Jr. and Eric Trump are advisers who stand to make tens of millions of dollars.
sub_claims.finding: Both sit on the strategic advisory board. Per Reuters, Eric received 3 million founder shares and Don Jr. 2 million. AP and Capital Brief valued the 5 million shares at about $50M on paper at the $10 IPO price, before the sons commit any capital of their own. That paper value depends on the SPAC completing a merger and on where the stock trades afterwards.

sub_claims.statement: The filing said the SPAC would leverage its strategic advisory board and management's industry relationships to generate a pipeline of deals.
sub_claims.finding: The advisory board (Trump Jr., Eric Trump, and Kyle Wool of Dominari) is confirmed, and the filing describes a competitive advantage drawn from management and affiliates. I could not find the exact phrase 'comprehensive industry relationships' in any accessible source, and sec.gov was blocked for direct fetch. The wording is typical SPAC boilerplate and is plausible.

sub_claims.statement: The filing said it would target companies well positioned to benefit from federal or state-level incentives such as government contracts or preferential procurement programs.
sub_claims.finding: AP and Bloomberg Law quote the original Aug. 4, 2025 S-1 as targeting a firm 'well-positioned to benefit from federal or state-level incentives, such as grants, tax credits, government contracts or preferential procurement programs.' The video's quote leaves out 'grants, tax credits'. I could not confirm that the follow-on phrase about 'sectors where the U.S. government has an identifiable economic or security interest' was in the filing.

sub_claims.statement: Some of that language was removed later the same day.
sub_claims.finding: An amended S-1 filed later on Aug. 4, 2025 removed the incentives sentence and other descriptions, after AP asked the Trump Organization about the apparent conflict of interest. Outside counsel Paul Hastings told AP the sentence was a 'mistake' by 'scriveners'. Ethics experts noted that the amended filing still refers to targets that can benefit from 'public policy tailwinds'. 'Some' is therefore the right word: the incentives sentence went, but the policy-tailwind framing stayed.

sub_claims.statement: Implied: the Trump sons' advisory role gives the SPAC an edge in winning government contracts (for example, by calling the Pentagon).
sub_claims.finding: This is the video's inference. It ties the SPAC to an earlier interview quote about strategic investors calling the Pentagon. No search result shows a business combination target for NWAX or any contact with an agency. As of the latest reporting I could find, no merger had been announced, and low-quality aggregator pages dated 2026 could not be verified. The conflict-of-interest concern is documented: Kathleen Clark said, 'They just deleted the language. They haven't committed not to do what they said earlier today they were planning to do.' Specific misuse of influence is not documented. Audit (Nov 2026): no definitive business-combination agreement or named target was found. A Feb 6, 2026 8-K reports one director resignation and two new directors. Third-party summaries put the liquidation deadline at June 5, 2027, extendable, but that is unverified against the charter.

corrections: The transcript says the SPAC 'has been raising three hundred million dollars'. It filed for $300M in August 2025, priced at $300M on Dec. 3, 2025, and closed at $345M after the over-allotment was exercised.

The video's quote of the filing omits 'grants, tax credits'. The original reads 'federal or state-level incentives, such as grants, tax credits, government contracts or preferential procurement programs.'
The sons' 'tens of millions' is about $50M in paper value from 5 million founder shares (3M Eric, 2M Don Jr.) at $10. It is not realized cash, and it depends on a completed merger.
The auto-transcript's 'New American acquisition, one corp' is New America Acquisition I Corp (NYSE: NWAX).
denials_and_context: The filing's law firm, Paul Hastings, called the incentives sentence a scrivener's 'mistake'. A company spokesperson called it a clerical error.
The Trump Organization did not answer AP's question about whether New America still planned to benefit from government programs.
The amended filing still talks about 'public policy tailwinds' and revitalizing domestic manufacturing and critical supply chains, so the government-policy angle was not dropped entirely.

The Trump brothers are also large shareholders in Dominari Holdings, whose broker-dealer co-underwrote the IPO and whose president, Kyle Wool, sits on the advisory board. The same Dominari partnership is behind American Bitcoin.

Founder shares bought for a nominal price and worth millions are standard in SPACs. What is unusual is the sitting president's sons as advisers combined with the government-incentives targeting language.

leads.title: Dominari Holdings: Trump sons' stake in the broker that underwrote their SPAC
leads.why_connected: The Trump brothers are major Dominari shareholders. Dominari Securities co-underwrote NWAX, and its president sits on the SPAC's board, so the sons may profit on both sides of the deal. Dominari is also the origin of American Bitcoin.

leads.why_connected: An earlier 2025 SPAC deal with Don Jr. on the board of a firearms retailer, a sector shaped by federal regulation. The video did not cover it.
